cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and it's from David. He's thinking back to the day they said to him, 'Let us go to the house of the LORD.' Now friend, you know that moment when somebody invites you somewhere and your FACE answers before your mouth does.

cards.question: When they invite David to go to the house of the LORD, David says he was ___.

cards.text: Then they've made it, and David says, 'Our feet are standing…' Must be NICE having feet, friend, because I've been hopping around on a gold base my whole life.

cards.question: David and the people with him have arrived. Where does David say their feet are standing?

answers.text: At the foot of Mount Sinai

cards.text: David looks around at the city he's standing in. And he says something about the way it's built.

cards.question: Standing in Jerusalem, how does David describe the way the city is built?

answers.text: As a city of gold and cedar
As a city hidden in the hills

cards.text: Jerusalem is where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony for Israel. Friend, I've watched a group chat argue for three DAYS over where to meet, and here come whole tribes, all headed for the same city.

cards.question: The tribes of the LORD go up to Jerusalem to give thanks to the name of the LORD.

cards.text: David's got one more thing to say about this city. Jerusalem isn't only where the tribes come to give thanks.

cards.question: David says the thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David, stand in Bethlehem.

cards.text: Then David stops describing the city. Now he gives an instruction.

cards.question: David gives an instruction about Jerusalem. What does he say to pray for?

cards.text: And David even gives the words to pray, starting with who should prosper. Thank goodness, because left to me it'd just be, 'Uh… good stuff for Jerusalem… amen?'

cards.question: The prayer David gives asks for those who rule Jerusalem to prosper.
The prayer for Jerusalem goes on: may there be ___ within your walls, and prosperity inside your fortresses.

cards.text: Then David makes a promise: he will say, 'Peace be within you.' Man, I could've used that line in the junk drawer, with the dead batteries I shared it with arguing ALL night over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: David promises to say to Jerusalem, Peace be within you. Why does he say he'll do it?

answers.text: For the sake of his brothers and friends
To win the favor of the crowds
Because the elders asked him to

cards.text: Then comes the last line of the song. And it lands right back where David started.

cards.question: For the sake of the ___ of the LORD our God, David says he will seek Jerusalem's ___.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin has been 'hopping around on a gold base my whole life.' In his backstory, the gold base came only when he was renewed in the Dorinverse. Before that he spent years as a stamper in the Millers' kitchen and the junk drawer. The line adds something new to his story that contradicts it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says, 'I've watched a group chat argue for three DAYS over where to meet.' This claims a personal experience with a group chat. His story is the Millers' kitchen, the junk drawer and the Dorinverse. The docs say he knows everyday adult life for comparisons, but they don't say whether he can claim he took part in it or saw it himself.
findings.question: When Papa Dorin makes an everyday-life comparison, can he say he personally saw or did the modern thing ("I've watched a group chat…")? Or must he frame it without claiming the experience ("You know when a group chat…")?

findings.problem: The card cites Psalm 122:5 but tells nothing from verse 5. Its only content restates verse 4 (the tribes coming to give thanks), which works as a recap of the answer to card 8.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card mostly repeats what card 8 just established ('Jerusalem isn't only where the tribes come to give thanks') instead of moving the psalm forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Several story cards are bare signposts with no Papa Dorin voice and almost no passage content. Card 5 ('says something about the way it's built'), card 9, card 11 ('Now he gives an instruction') and card 18 read as plain transitions, not as Papa Dorin telling the psalm.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 16 calls David's words a promise ('David makes a promise'), and card 17 repeats it ('David promises to say'). The text says only 'I will say.' It never calls this a promise.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The setup says the last line 'lands right back where David started.' The psalm started with 'the house of the LORD' (verse 1), so this hands the baker blank 1 ('house') on card 19.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
